facts.text: The default robot is google_robot_static
The static Google robot's default control mode is arm_pd_ee_delta_pose_align_interpolate_by_planner_gripper_pd_joint_target_delta_pos_interpolate_by_planner
The arm pose controller builds a six-element Box: three position deltas and three rotation deltas
The arm controller config passes pos_lower -1.0, pos_upper 1.0 and rot_bound np.pi / 2
The selected arm explicitly disables action normalization, retaining its rotation Box bounds
The controller normalizes its action space when normalize_action is true
The action normalizer is Box(-1, 1) with the original shape and dtype
The gripper uses PDJointPosMimicControllerConfig with normalize_action=True
CombinedController flattens the arm and gripper spaces into one Box
GraspSingleCokeCanInScene-v0 is registered with max_episode_steps=80 and the model_ids list ['coke_can']
register_env notes that gym.make wraps the environment with a TimeLimit to limit the maximum number of steps
The supported observation modes are state, state_dict, none and image
The default obs_mode is the first supported mode
For obs_mode state, get_obs flattens the observation dict into one array
The agent proprioception is qpos, qvel and the controller state
The static Google robot qpos is 11-dimensional
The observation adds the robot base pose to the agent proprioception
The task adds tcp_pose, obj_pose and tcp_to_obj_pos to the state observation
A serialized pose is its position followed by its quaternion, seven numbers
The reward is 0.0, or 1.0 when the episode info has success
The episode terminates when info['success'] is true
reset(seed, options) reseeds the main and episode RNGs and initializes the episode
The scene timestep is 1 / sim_freq
sim_freq defaults to 500 Hz and control_freq to 20 Hz
BaseEnv get_state returns actor/articulation simulation state and requires task-specific overrides
Task success depends on consecutive grasp, lifted state and episode statistics
Reset settles actors by integrating the scene
The native control loop calls scene.step once per configured simulation substep
The substep count is sim_freq // control_freq; the separately cited 500 Hz and 20 Hz defaults give 25
BaseEnv provides get_state and set_state for the simulation state
BaseEnv seeds its main RNG with 2022 before it constructs the environment
step_action calls scene.step and then _after_simulation_step once per simulation substep
The sim_timestep property is 1.0 / _sim_freq
_settle steps the scene int(sim_freq * t) times
The object settles with _settle(0.5) twice and _settle(1.5) once more when it is still moving
EnvSpec.make passes the registered default keyword arguments to the environment class

determinism.notes: The fake Python RNG and native NumPy RNG differ; no cross-backend trajectory or exact native determinism is claimed.

gaps: Package-owned 48-number state stand-in; values are test data, not native observations.
No SAPIEN, contacts, PD drives, rendered scene, asset loading or physical device is simulated.
One fake tick is a logical 50 ms control interval. No physical substeps are integrated.
The selected live defaults use 500 Hz physics and 20 Hz control, or 25 substeps per control call.
The fake models the 80-control-step TimeLimit; the raw native task terminates on success.
JSON snapshots capture the fake's state and Python RNG, not native SAPIEN or NumPy state.
Only the default state observation and seven-axis control are exposed; no image observations.
No wall-clock pacing or comparison against the native simulator or hardware.

safe_state.description: No new step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch. A native step or reset already running is not interrupted: it completes (a multi-step command stops at the next control call), and the e-stop reports the safe state only after it ended, waiting at most the e-stop budget and otherwise retrying in the background. The world state stays readable.
